title: One Breath Left - Derelicts and Danger!
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n9XvIj6hOjc

Daniel (@dungeondive) takes a look at One Breath Left from Stout Stoat, a procedurally generated solo journaling game about exploring an abandoned spaceship that he stumbled on while hunting for small science-fiction games. It uses no dice. Every action, whether peering through a door, moving or searching, costs one breath from an oxygen track, and each ship's peril events are circled on that track in advance so disaster arrives on schedule. Rooms are drawn from a deck and laid into a map; each has a search track whose numbered nodes trigger events in the navigation guide and whose circles yield clues. Five explorers, five contracts and five ship conditions (breached, infected, raided, shifted, stalked) combine for variety, and a legacy system hands tools and clues to your next character.

The writing, he says, is far more evocative than a box of three little booklets suggests, and he sees it as a perfect companion to Space Aces: that game for flying and fighting, this one for the moment you board a derelict. He plays a young Sam Foyle on the breached research vessel Intractable, finding a biometric scanner in the medical bay, a toy in the crew quarters that comes alive in his pocket, an emergency bulkhead sealing off his airlock, and, behind some gallons of space milk in the commissary, one last bottle of Captain Weinhardt's Root Beer. He escapes by pod. Cozy, effortless and fulfilling is his verdict.

----

One Breath Left has no dice, just a breath counter and prompts. Can a game with no randomiser at all still generate real tension for you?
